SUBJECT:  CONSIDERATION OF EMPLOYEE GRIEVANCE NO. 20-07

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council deny Grievance No. 20-07 on the grounds that
the grievance does not state a claim or claims for the City Council to act upon in that
grievance fails to identify: (1) the grievants; (2) the facts and/or allegations underlying
the grievance; (3) the manner in which the MOU has allegedly been violated; and (4)
the persons at the City who purportedly engaged in behavior that violated the MOU.

BACKGROUND

Under the Brown Act, personnel grievances may be heard in closed session for City
Council consideration where an identified employee or employees has grieved specific
complaints and charges that sufficiently identify the underlying facts so as to determine
whom the allegations are against and what is the basis of the accusation. The purpose
of allowing these personnel discussions in closed session is to protect the confidential
personnel rights of employees and to permit a free and candid discussion of personnel
matters by a local government body. However, where the requirements for the
personnel exception for closed session are not met, the City Council is not permitted to
hear the matter in closed session, in accordance with the Brown Act.

At the same time, however, the City Council (1) cannot discuss in open session matters
that pertain to the confidential personnel information of an employee or employees
(without the employee(s) waiving his/her/their rights), and (2) must be presented with
grievances so as to be able to take action, in accordance with Step 4 of the grievance
process under the Rank and File MOU.

Accordingly, because a grievance must contain sufficient information in order to satisfy
the Brown Act's requirements for the personnel exception to be heard in closed session
(Gov. Code sec. 54957) and the City has still not been provided with such information,
because confidential personnel matters cannot be discussed in open session, and
because the City Council must be presented with grievances under Step 4 of the
grievance process under the Rank and File MOU, this matter has been placed on the

  consent calendar in order to allow City Council action, while simultaneously adhering to
  the Brown Act and minimizing discussion to protect confidential employee personnel
  information.

  DISCUSSION

  In accordance with Step 4 of the grievance process under the Rank and File MOU,
  Grievance No. 20-07 is being brought forth for City Council action.

  However, it is not apparent from the face of Grievance No. 20-07 who the grievance is
  on behalf of, what facts or allegations of wrongdoing underlie the grievance, how such
  actions would purportedly violate the MOU, or who at the City would purportedly have
  taken such actions. This information is necessary both for the City to be able to
  agendize the matter under the personnel exception for closed session in accordance
  with the Brown Act and for the City to be able to know how to prepare for the City
  Council grievance hearing.

  At the Union's behest, the City placed Grievance No. 20-07 on the City Council's open
  session agenda for the September 8, 2020 City Council meeting for City Council
  consideration. 1 The City requested multiple times from AFSCME representatives that
  the above-referenced necessary information be provided. AFSCME representatives
  declined to provide any such information. Accordingly, at the September 8th meeting, the
  matter was continued by the City Council in order to again provide the Union more time
  to present this requisite information so that the City Council could properly hear the
  matter. The City must be able to prepare for the grievance hearings by knowing which
  employees are grieving the matter and what the underlying facts and allegations are
  (including how the MOU was purportedly violated and who allegedly did so). The City
  needs to protect the confidential personnel information of its employees, which it cannot
  do in open session if it is unaware of which employees may be discussed during a
  grievance proceeding and whether such employees have consented to such discussion.

  This information again was requested of AFSCME representatives after the September
  8th meeting, and AFSCME representatives were further notified that if such information
  was not provided, the grievance would be placed on the consent calendar on a future
  City Council agenda with a recommendation of denial for failure to state a claim, as set
  forth above. As of the writing of this staff report, no additional information was provided
  by the Union.

  It is therefore recommended that the City Council deny Grievance No. 20-07 on the
  basis that it fails to state a claim or claims for the City Council to act upon in that
  grievance does not identify: (1) the grievants; (2) the facts and/or allegations underlying
  the grievance; (3) the manner in which the MOU has allegedly been violated; and (4) the
  persons at the City who purportedly engaged in behavior that violated the MOU.

1 Under the Brown Act, moving a personnel exception matter into open session first requires that the matter be
appropriately agendized for closed session. (See Gov. Code sec. 54957.) That was not the case here.
